title: Revelations About Payments to Kassio Nunes Marques' Son
seoTitle: Revelations About Payments to Kassio Nunes Marques' Son
subtitle: Cell phone dialogue and Master case investigation put the minister in focus
excerpt: Extracted phone chats show monthly payments of R$500,000 to lawyer Kevin Marques, son of Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, sparking controversy.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Conversations found on banker Daniel Vorcaro's phone, former controller of Banco Master, revealed monthly payments of R$500,000 to lawyer Kevin Marques, the son of Minister Kassio Nunes Marques. The release of the messages coincided with a plenary session of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) that will consider authorising an investigation against Minister Alexandre de Moraes.

What the messages between Vorcaro and Master say

In August 2025, the then legal director of Banco Master, Luiz Rennó Netto, sent Vorcaro a contact for Kevin Marques and wrote that "a payment to 'consult' is missing." In another July 2025 message, Rennó asked whether the "R$500,000 per month" transfer to the lawyer should continue, to which Vorcaro replied with "kkkk."

Payments to Consult Inteligência Tributária

A report by Estado de S.Paulo indicated that Consult Inteligência Tributária paid Kevin Marques R$281.6 thousand for specialized legal services in the administrative tax area. Kevin's firm stated that he never rendered services to Banco Master nor received money from Vorcaro, acknowledging only the receipt from Consult.

Reaction of Minister Kassio Nunes Marques

In a statement, Minister Kassio Nunes Marques declared that he never voted in favour of Banco Master and that his son never received money from Daniel Vorcaro. The text explained that the minister's vote in a case concerning compensation for sugar‑cane‑alcohol plants was cast while he served as vice‑president of TRF‑1, and that the decision had no direct link to Master.

STF plenary and Moraes investigation

The conversations surfaced a few hours before the plenary session in which the STF will decide whether to authorise an investigation into Minister Alexandre de Moraes for his relationship with Vorcaro. The plenary will assess whether 52 exchanged messages between Vorcaro and Moraes constitute a minimal indication to launch a probe.

Position of André Mendonça

Minister André Mendonça, the rapporteur of the inquiry, denied any irregularities in the conduct of the investigation. In a statement presented to the Court's president, Edson Fachin, Mendonça explained that he ordered the Federal Police to identify the people mentioned in Vorcaro's dialogues and that the summons of investigators was carried out in person to preserve the integrity of the proceedings.

Conclusion of the current scenario

The Master case, by involving payments to Kevin Marques and the possible influence of STF members, has raised discussions about the Federal Police's handling of investigations and the role of ministers in assessing potential conflicts of interest. The decisions made in the plenary will define the next steps of the inquiry and may affect public perception of judicial independence.

With information from O GLOBO, Estadão.
